clue.text: Mayo, perhaps, meeting possible GAA opponents in tie? Probably not

definitions.note: a phrase describing someone choosing casual clothes, so unlikely to be wearing a tie

parts.note: mayonnaise, mayo for short, is an example of a salad dressing
Down is a county with a Gaelic football side in the Gaelic Athletic Association, a possible opponent for County Mayo

explanation.surface: An Irish sports report wondering whether County Mayo will face a rival county in a cup tie, and doubting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mayo' and 'tie' look like Gaelic football, a cup tie between counties; the definition instead takes 'tie' as the neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing informally means leaving the necktie at home, so a person in casual clothes is probably not in a tie.

clue.text: Pop article in with large cups

indicators.note: in says the article is set inside the cup size letters

parts.note: DD is a large bra cup size
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shopping note: a news item about a lingerie line with big cup sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal word for a father, as is this three-letter synonym.

clue.text: Calling time?

parts.note: read as time paying a visit: time, the old foe, calling at the house and knocking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling time' suggests a publican announcing last orders; instead 'calling' means visiting, and time is the traditional foe that comes knocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe on the threshold is one who has come calling, and time is proverbially the enemy of all of us.

clue.text: Woman left, initially forgotten here?

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word forgotten

explanation.surface: A wistful question about where an unmarried woman ends up, forgotten from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a woman 'left on the shelf' has been passed over, forgotten, there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'left on the shelf' describes a woman thought past marrying, overlooked and forgotten in that place.

clue.text: Time off in Scotland?

definitions.meaning: a particular time of day, twelve o'clock midday
in Scots 'no' means 'not', so '...' is a Scottish way of saying not on, that is off

explanation.walkthrough: Scots English uses 'no' for 'not' ('I'm no going'), so split as NO ON the answer reads as Scots for 'not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a specific time, and in Scots dialect the split phrase means 'not on', switched off.

clue.text: Light lifted and switched on by a North American

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an LED, light-emitting diode, is a light
switched on means alert, aware

explanation.surface: Someone from North America picks up a lamp and turns it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the US state of Delaware is an American.

clue.text: Roller might, if harnessed?

parts.note: a roller is a big breaking sea wave, and its might is its force, which can be put to use generating electricity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' suggests a Rolls-Royce or a hair roller, and 'harnessed' a horse; here it is the sea's breakers whose strength is tapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy taken from the motion of ocean breakers is a form of renewable electricity generation.

clue.text: Not easy: when to stop men pestering women athletes

parts.note: a steep task is a hard one

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so this word sits inside the next

parts.note: lechers are men who make unwanted advances to women
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A complaint about when harassment of female athletes will finally end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' plugs the word for 'when' into the men's word; 'Not easy' looks like a comment, but it opens the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners in the obstacle race with hurdles and water jumps are athletes.

clue.text: Like Barnet for Conservative Women's Red Line Bus excursion

definitions.note: Barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and a bluish tint is the stereotypical hairdo of older Tory women; past-tense adjective

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering trip, so these letters go off on a new route

explanation.surface: A London borough laying on a red bus outing for its Conservative women's group.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the north London borough, but is Cockney rhyming slang for hair. Blue is the Conservative party colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair given a bluish tinting rinse is a stock image of the elderly female Tory activist.

clue.text: Fuel to finish — and plug boxes call for attention

parts.note: to die is to come to an end, to finish

indicators.note: boxes means holds inside, so the call goes within the promotion word

parts.note: to plug a product is to promote or sell it
oi is a shout to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: A garage or advert scene: a final push of a product, with someone shouting to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy oil burnt in compression-ignition engines is a vehicle fuel.

clue.text: Lively one Klitschko finally cut down to size

indicators.note: the brother's name loses its final letter, trimmed short

parts.note: Vitali Klitschko is one of the two Ukrainian boxing brothers, now mayor of Kyiv

explanation.surface: A lively heavyweight boxer finally brought down to size by an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Klitschko brothers, Vitali and Wladimir, were heavyweight boxing champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital in the sense full of energy and life is a synonym for lively.

clue.text: Get back at the conclusion of work and settle

definitions.text: Get back at the conclusion of work
definitions.meaning: a lump sum received when leaving a job, a final payment on dismissal
to clear a debt in full

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back at' looks like revenge; the first definition is the money you get on leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a final payment made at the end of employment; the verb phrase means to settle a debt.

clue.text: Weak captive bloodshot after rising blow

parts.note: POW stands for prisoner of war, a captive

indicators.note: after rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: bloodshot eyes are red
to puff is to blow

explanation.surface: A weak prisoner, eyes bloodshot after getting up, takes a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, feeble thing or person is called by this cosmetic pad's name, so it means weak.

clue.text: Suite, for example, that's over still spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of says the words are said aloud, and a sound-alike gives the entry

parts.note: over means too (too much), and still means peace, quiet calm

explanation.surface: Furniture talk: a suite that is still being discussed though it is old news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' reads as furniture; a furniture suite is often sold as matching pieces, here two.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa-and-chair set sold as a two-item set is one kind of furniture suite, so the definition gives an example.

clue.text: Agent, quietly raising gym exercise without good mental preparation

indicators.note: raising in a down clue lifts the quiet letter higher, to the start of the agent word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
P stands for piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: without means outside, so the exercise wraps round the letter

parts.note: a chin-up is a gym exercise lifting the body to a bar

explanation.surface: A secret agent quietly doing gym work, but without any good mental preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raising' lifts the quiet letter to the top of the agent word; 'without' means outside, wrapping the exercise round the good letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting oneself mentally ready for a challenge is the phrasal verb's sense, a form of mental readiness.

clue.text: Wife burns tongue shifting man's potion

parts.note: itches means stings or burns

indicators.note: shifting means removing the man pronoun from the language name

parts.note: Hebrew is a language, a tongue
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A wife's tongue burns from a man's potion she has drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like part of the mouth, scalded; it is the language Hebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: A concoction stirred in a cauldron by hags is a magic potion.

clue.text: Over-familiar, rough and cheeky

indicators.note: rough means roughed up, disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A description of someone over-familiar: rough-mannered and cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough and cheeky' reads as a second definition, but 'rough' is the anagram signal on AND CHEEKY.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used so often it feels stale is trite, too familiar from overuse.

clue.text: This flower arrangement certainly would be easy

indicators.note: would be says this word joined with the next makes a longer one, so take that word away

parts.note: leisurely means unhurried, easy
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: A florist assures us that this arrangement would be easy to make.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'This (flower arrangement) + certainly would be easy': this word followed by SURELY makes LEISURELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck is a flower arrangement.

clue.text: Can't stand after removal of a flipping thorn? Something like that!

definitions.note: thorn is an old English letter; this is a similar one, a letter from the same alphabet

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
after removal of means the article is dropped from the word

parts.note: to hate is to be unable to stand something

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated with a flipping thorn bush they can't stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Deleting A from HATE leaves HTE; 'flipping' turns it round. 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse; 'thorn' looks like a prickle but is the runic letter þ.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn and its partner ð are both Old English letters for the 'th' sound.

clue.text: Monsters of Rock is restored with Alice Cooper initially, etc.

indicators.note: restored means put back together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letters of the singer's two names

explanation.surface: The Monsters of Rock festival returns with shock-rocker Alice Cooper and other acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Monsters of Rock was a heavy metal festival; Alice Cooper is a shock-rock singer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are mythical serpents hatched from a cock's egg, able to kill with a look: monsters.

clue.text: Poet cycling in photograph like old woman?

indicators.note: in puts the cycled poet inside the photograph word

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photograph

indicators.note: cycling means the poet's last letter goes round to the front

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a poet out cycling, looking like an old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' turns DANTE into EDANT. 'Old woman' is a disparaging term for a fussy, nitpicking person of either sex, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called an old woman is fussy over petty detail, which is being overly precise and nitpicking.

clue.text: Accessible series of Jonathan Dimbleby's

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A TV listing: a broadcaster's programme series is available to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Dimbleby is a British broadcaster who presented the BBC radio series Any Questions?.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by and ready to use is accessible, the idiom meaning near enough to reach.

clue.text: Fighter mounted on horse, yet disappearing every second

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means going up, so the letters read backwards
every other letter of these words drops out, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: A fighter on horseback, yet vanishing at every moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters of 'on horse yet' are N, O, S, Y, T; 'mounted' reads them upwards. Mike Tyson is the heavyweight boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson, former world heavyweight champion, is a famous fighter in the boxing ring.

clue.text: Caribbean houses provided that internet facility

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the condition word sits within

parts.note: WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Caribbean holiday homes offering wireless internet access.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless networking that connects devices to the internet is an internet facility.

clue.text: Reading down at one point score twice instead in this?

definitions.text: Reading down at one point score twice instead in this?
definitions.note: a match in which Reading FC, behind at one stage, then score twice: a football match

indicators.note: instead means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a score is twenty, so twice that is forty
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs
a side that is down at one point has nil, O, on the scoreboard

explanation.surface: A comeback: Reading FC behind at one stage, then scoring twice in a game of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English football club. In FORTY, the R is swapped for O, a nil score. The whole clue pictures a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A game in which Reading trail, then net two goals, is association football, informally so called in Britain.

clue.text: Politician's one time to talk cases with Holmes briefly

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the talk word wraps round the letters

parts.note: to gas is to chatter, talk
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Kelly Holmes is the British double Olympic champion runner

explanation.surface: A politician takes time to discuss cases with Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holmes' and 'cases' suggest Sherlock; the Holmes here is Dame Kelly. Hugh Gaitskell led the UK Labour Party 1955-63.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Gaitskell was a Labour Party leader and Chancellor of the Exchequer, a British politician.

clue.text: Man has feet in bowl — pure bliss!

indicators.note: feet in a down clue are the bottom letters, the last letters of the words

explanation.surface: A man soaks his feet in a bowl of water: sheer bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, short for Leslie, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Points said to upset Christian heretics

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman's charge that heretics distort the points the church has made.
explanation.definitionFit: These were followers of an early belief that Christ was God's son only by adoption, condemned as heresy.
